lc_steward.text: Six medieval queens owned this castle in their own right, starting with Eleanor of Castile in 1278. It was a gift kings gave their wives. Better than flowers.
Henry VIII turned it into a palace for Catherine of Aragon. He came through on his way to meet the King of France at the Field of the Cloth of Gold in 1520, with five thousand people in tow.
The historian Lord Conway called it 'the loveliest castle in the world'. We put that on everything. Wouldn't you?

lc_dogcollar.text: There's a museum of dog collars here! Hundreds of years of them, some with spikes against wolves. I came for the castle. I'm staying for the collars.
